errors.problem: The sentence-initial imperative has no vowel on its hamzat-waṣl alif, so the engine reads it as Inẓurū ('Inẓurū ilā hādhihi sh-sharīḥa'). The verb is نَظَرَ / يَنْظُرُ (u-stem), so the imperative starts with u: unẓurū. A learner is taught the wrong pronunciation.
errors.alsoChange: tap key for the form; transliteration becomes Unẓurū automatically

errors.problem: The kasra is written on the silent hamzat-waṣl alif after al-. The helping vowel belongs on the lām (al-ithnayn = الِاثْنَيْن), which is how the course writes every other al- + waṣl word (الِامْتِحَان, الِاسْتِقْبَال, الِاجْتِمَاعِيّ). Inconsistent spelling of the headword for Monday.
errors.alsoChange: tap key الاِثْنَيْن → الِاثْنَيْن in the glossary

errors.problem: The note gives أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ '(where do you live?, to a man)', but tapping تَسْكُنُ shows '(she) lives'. The learner gets the wrong person in the very phrase the note teaches.
errors.alsoChange: only for this note: the examples of [314] and [316] (Sami's aunt / my aunt Huda lives) correctly need 'she lives'

errors.problem: In مَا فَعَلْتُ شَيْئًا يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة ('I didn't do anything on Friday') مَا is the negation of a past verb, not 'what'. The gloss makes the sentence read 'What did I do something on Friday'. Reported in round 1 and still there.
errors.alsoChange: line-level override only; مَا=what is right everywhere else

errors.problem: In the headword's own example 'as far as the traffic lights' the word is glossed 'pointing'. Reported in round 1 and still there.
ثَلَاثَ مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم is 'three times a day'; the tap makes it 'three times today'. Reported in round 1 and still there.
errors.alsoChange: line-level override only; الْيَوْم=today is right in most other lines

errors.problem: عَلَى الْمَكْتَب مِصْبَاح جَدِيد is translated 'On the desk there is a new lamp', but the tap says 'the office' ('on the office').
سِعْرُ اللَّيْلَة خَمْسُونَ دِينَارًا is 'the price for one night is fifty dinars' (per night), not 'the price of tonight'.
In الْجَوّ هُنَاكَ دَافِئ حَتَّى فِي الشِّتَاء ('warm even in winter') حَتَّى means 'even'. 'until' gives 'warm until in winter'.
الْكُتُبُ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ الْإِنْتَرْنِت is a comparison with مِنْ: 'books are better than the internet' (as the English says). 'the best' teaches the wrong reading of the elative + min.
أَعْرِفُ أَنَّهَا تُحِبُّ أَغَانِيَ أُمِّ كُلْثُوم: the subject is 'she' (أَنَّهَا), as the English says ('she loves'). The tap gives 'you like (to a man)'.
In the greeting رَمَضَان كَرِيم ('Ramadan is generous', as the note itself says) كَرِيم is the adjective 'generous', not the name Karim. Reported in round 1 and still there.
errors.alsoChange: line-level override; 'Karim (first name)' is right in [64].note, [69].example.ar and [606].example.ar

errors.problem: The plural of رَجُل (man) is glossed with the sign sense 'men (toilets)'. In the vocabulary entry it is simply 'men'. Reported in round 1 and still there.
errors.alsoChange: keep 'men (toilets)' only on the placard where it is a sign

errors.problem: As the plural of سَيِّد, سَادَة means 'gentlemen, sirs' (السَّادَة …). The gloss belongs to the colloquial coffee word (qahwa sāda). Reported in round 1 and still there.
غَدًا رِحْلَتُنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ is 'tomorrow is our trip to the beach' (as translated). 'our flight' to a beach is wrong; the trip sense is the main one of رِحْلَة.

errors.current: أَوَّلَ=the first (of): with 'yesterday', the day before yesterday
errors.problem: In أَتَذَكَّرُ أَوَّلَ دَرْسٍ ('I remember the first lesson') the tap explains 'the day before yesterday', a sense that belongs only to أَوَّلَ أَمْسِ.
errors.alsoChange: keep the long gloss only for [340] and the [321] note (أَوَّلَ أَمْسِ)

errors.problem: In يُقَالُ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا ('this clock never worked') السَّاعَةَ is the clock, in -a because of إِنَّ. 'at the hour' is a time adverb from another sentence and wrong here. Reported in round 1 and still there.

إِنَّ الْأَخْبَارَ الْيَوْمَ جَيِّدَة opens the sentence: here إِنَّ is the emphatic 'indeed' (the news today is good), not 'that' after qāla. There is no qāla in the sentence, so the learner is told a false rule for this line.
errors.fix: إِنَّ=indeed (stresses the sentence; noun after it in -a)
errors.alsoChange: 'that (after qāla)' stays right in [721] and in the notes of [664] and [721]

errors.problem: صَنَعَ is the active verb 'he made', as the label says; the gloss begins 'was made', the passive meaning of صُنِعَ. Reported in round 1 and still there.
Same fault as صَنَعَ: the active اِكْتَشَفَ ('he discovered') is glossed 'was discovered', the passive of اُكْتُشِفَ.

Systematic: a form with no gloss of its own gets the headword's gloss with the form label appended, without changing the tense or person. So present forms read as past (يَطْبُخُ=cooked (present), يُشَاهِدُ=saw, watched (present), يَسْمَعُ=heard (present)), past forms read as present (فَتَحَ=opens (past), تَنَفَّسَ=breathes (past), شَعَرَ=feels (past), أَعْلَنَتْ=announces (she, past), عُدْتُ=returns, goes back (I, past)), imperatives and 1st/2nd persons read as 3rd person (نَامِي=sleeps (order, to a woman), اُرْكُضْ=runs (order, to a man), أَرْتَاحُ=rests (I, present), تَفْتَحُ=opens (you, present)), verbal nouns read as verbs (حِمَايَة=protects (verbal noun), مَنْع=bans, forbids (noun: a ban, banning)), and present passives read as past (يُبْنَى=was built (present passive, it is built), قِيلَ=it is said (past passive, it was said)). About 105 taps in this chunk. The meaning is guessable, but the English contradicts the form the learner is studying.
errors.alsoChange: compose the gloss from the form itself: past = '(he) Xed', present = 'he Xes', I-form = 'I X', you-form = 'you X', order = 'X! (to …)', verbal noun = the English noun (protection, saving, ban), present passive = 'is Xed'. Or write the gloss by hand for each forms[] entry, as is already done for most of days 1–6.

errors.problem: شَابَّة is 'young woman'; 'young man (feminine)' is an auto-composed contradiction. Reported in round 1 and still there.
The entry teaches 'to get off; to go down' (example: أَيْنَ أَنْزِلُ؟ 'where do I get off?'), but tapping the headword shows 'falls, comes down'. Still there from round 1.
errors.alsoChange: 'comes down, falls' can stay for the snow sentences in [467] and [476]

errors.problem: Under the travel entry 'weight', the plural is glossed with the grammar sense 'patterns'. Still there from round 1.
In أُرِيدُ سَلَطَةً خَضْرَاء the -an is the object of 'I want'; there is no لَيْسَ. The grammar tag belongs to another sentence. Still there from round 1.
In أُرِيدُ قَمِيصًا جَمِيلًا the -an is agreement with the object قَمِيصًا; there is no kāna. Wrong grammar tag for this line.
In أَعْلَنَتِ الْحُكُومَةُ عُطْلَةً the -an marks the object of 'announced'; there is no 'was'.

The verb in these lines is يَكُونُ ('is usually'), not كَانَ: the tag 'after was' tells the learner the sentence is past. Same fault in [470].example.ar: حَارًّا=hot (after 'was') in فِي الصَّيْف يَكُونُ الْجَوّ حَارًّا.
In أَرْجُو أَنْ تَرُدَّ عَلَيَّ قَرِيبًا the verb ends in -a because of أَنْ; after lam it would be the jussive. The tag teaches the wrong mood.
In أَرْجُو أَنْ تَرُدَّ عَلَيَّ قَرِيبًا ('reply to me soon') قَرِيبًا is the time adverb 'soon'.
In اِفْتَحُوا الْكِتَابَ the -a is the object of the imperative; there is no أَنَّ.

عَشَرَ is glossed 'part of fifteen' in sentences that say twelve (اِثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا), the nineteenth (التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ), the eighteenth (الثَّامِنَ عَشَرَ) and the twelfth (الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ) century.
errors.fix: عَشَرَ=ten (second part of a number from 11 to 19)

errors.problem: The form is labelled 'you (present)' (and the entry is about a doctor speaking to a patient), but the tap says 'sits (she, it)'.
errors.fix: تَجْلِسُ=you sit (to a man); she sits

errors.problem: The form is labelled 'she (present)', but the tap says 'you write (to a man)'. Label and gloss disagree.
errors.fix: تَكْتُبُ=she writes; you write (to a man)

errors.problem: In the entry 'pharmacist', forms[0] is labelled 'feminine' (a woman pharmacist), but the tap shows only 'pharmacy, chemist's'.
In 'The adjective after it ends in ـًا' the ending is the -an tanwīn (fatḥatān on a seat alif), the point of the note. Calling it 'the letter alif' hides the -an sound.
errors.fix: ـًا=-an (tanwīn fatḥa on alif: the accusative ending)

errors.problem: The singulative (one item) is glossed with the collective plural meaning plus a bracket: 'eggs (one egg)'. Same in مَوْزَة=bananas (one banana) [180].forms[0].ar, [180].note; بُرْتُقَالَة=oranges (one orange) [181].forms[0].ar, [181].note; دَجَاجَة=chicken (one chicken) [151].forms[0].ar, [151].note. The note says 'one hen is دَجَاجَة'.
errors.alsoChange: مَوْزَة=a banana; بُرْتُقَالَة=an orange; دَجَاجَة=a hen, a chicken

errors.problem: The feminine adjective ثَانِيَة ('second') is glossed 'again', a sense that belongs to the adverb مَرَّةً ثَانِيَةً / ثَانِيَةً.
أَنَا جَاهِز تَمَامًا is 'I'm completely ready', as translated; 'exactly' is wrong here.
In جَدَّتِي كَبِيرَة فِي السِّنّ ('my grandmother is elderly') كَبِيرَة means 'old (of age)'; the tap gives only 'big'.
هَلْ أَنْتِ طَوِيلَة مِثْلَ أُمِّكِ؟ is 'Are you tall like your mother?'; the tap says 'long'.
In الطَّلَاقَةُ تَأْتِي مَعَ الْوَقْت the subject is the singular 'fluency': 'it comes'.
كُلُّ مَجْمُوعَة تُقَدِّمُ تَقْدِيمًا قَصِيرًا is 'every group gives a short presentation' — the entry's own sense 'presents, gives'. 'offers' belongs to the scholarship sentences.
The note says 'سَجَّلَ / يُسَجِّلُ (to record; to register)'; the tap shows the football sense 'scored'.
أَوَّلُ كَاتِبٍ عَرَبِيٍّ is 'the first Arab writer' (as translated); for a person the adjective is 'Arab', not 'Arabic'.
In الْمُوسِيقَى الْعَرَبِيَّة ('Arabic music') الْعَرَبِيَّة is the feminine adjective agreeing with music, not the noun 'the Arabic language'.
The note lists لَكَ, لَهُ, لَهَا as 'for you, for him, for her'; لَهُ is glossed 'it has', breaking the paradigm (لَهَا is glossed 'for her').
The headword يَصُومُ ('he fasts', en: fasts) shows the sentence-specific gloss '(they) fast (verb first: singular)' from the Ramadan example; on the headword and the 'present' form it is wrong.
errors.alsoChange: keep the long gloss only for [630].example.ar

errors.problem: اسْمَعُوا الْإِعْلَانَ فِي الْمَحَطَّة is 'listen to the announcement at the station' (as translated); 'advertisement' is the other sense.
In the headword عَلَامَات التَّرْقِيم ('punctuation marks') the tap shows the exam sense 'mark, grade'.

The 'won' bracket belongs to the Nobel-prize sentences; on the past form of 'to take' and in أَخَذَ عُمَر عِيدِيَّة مِنْ جَدَّتِهِ ('Omar got Eid money from his grandmother') it says Omar 'won' the money.
The 'succeeds' bracket belongs to the proverb مَنْ جَدَّ وَجَدَ; on the past form of 'to find' it is wrong.

notes.note: 'A hollow verb like كَانَ: before -tu the long ā becomes i: نِمْتُ' can be read as if كَانَ also gave i; كَانَ gives كُنْتُ (u). Consider 'A hollow verb, but with i: نِمْتُ (compare كُنْتُ)'.
كَانَ صَوْتُهُ سَرِيعًا جِدًّا 'His voice was very fast' is odd in both languages; كَانَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِسُرْعَة (he was speaking fast) would be natural.

Sentence-initial imperatives اسْمَعُوا / اسْتَمِعُوا are written without the kasra the course puts on other initial waṣl alifs (اِفْتَحُوا, اِجْلِسْ). The engine still reads them correctly with i; only انْظُرُوا is wrong (reported).
مُدَرَاء is the common modern plural of مُدِير; purists prefer مُدِيرُونَ. Fine to keep, could be mentioned.
'To win a prize is أَخَذَ جَائِزَة' is everyday usage; the standard MSA verb is فَازَ بِجَائِزَة, which the course teaches later (faza). A cross-reference would help.
تَغَيُّرِ الْمُنَاخ is quoted with a genitive -i out of context; the citation form is تَغَيُّرُ الْمُنَاخ.
'He was the first Arab writer…' translates هُوَ أَوَّلُ كَاتِبٍ (He is the first…); acceptable for a dead writer, but 'He is' matches the Arabic.
Many examples drop case endings mid-sentence (مِصْر بَلَد جَمِيل, عِنْدِي سُعَال فِي اللَّيْل) while later units write full endings; consistent with the pause convention, not reported.

summary: Read the whole vocabulary export (809 entries): every headword, plural, form, gender, example, note and every tap gloss. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: genders, plurals (broken and sound), verb paradigms, imperatives, jussives/subjunctives, number agreement, elatives and the passive forms are correct; I found only two spelling problems (انْظُرُوا without its u, read Inẓurū; الاِثْنَيْن with the kasra on the waṣl alif). The errors are almost all tap glosses. I checked 6,010 tap glosses; about 170 are wrong or misleading for their line: ~65 context errors (a gloss from another sentence's sense: مَا=what in a negative, الْإِشَارَة=pointing, اللَّيْلَة=tonight for 'per night', أَحْسَنُ=the best for 'better', تُحِبُّ=you like for 'she loves', رِحْلَتُنَا=our flight, أَوَّلَ='the day before yesterday' in 'the first lesson', السَّاعَةَ=at the hour for 'the clock', كَرِيم=Karim in رَمَضَان كَرِيم, سَادَة=plain coffee, رِجَال=men (toilets); plus grammar tags such as 'after laysa', 'after was', 'form after lam', 'part of fifteen' attached to lines where they are false), and ~105 auto-composed form glosses that keep the headword's tense/person and append the label (يَطْبُخُ=cooked (present), نَامِي=sleeps (order, to a woman), حِمَايَة=protects (verbal noun)), reported once as an engine finding. Several round-1 items are still present (مَا, الْإِشَارَة, فِي الْيَوْم, كَرِيم, السَّاعَةَ, رِجَال, سَادَة, أَوْزَان, يَنْزِلُ, شَابَّة, سَلَطَةً, صَنَعَ/اِكْتَشَفَ). Totals: 52 errors, 19 major (1 arabic, 18 gloss) and 33 minor (1 arabic, 31 gloss, 1 engine); 8 notes.
